pr_title: Quickly process unavailable metrics in Prometheus
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This fixes issue #133157, which became a performance problem after PR #125492.

The prometheus python client library has a mostly write-only interface. It is very difficult to extract most metadata about metrics.

In order to get information about stored metrics, the previous version of this code ran a full collection cycle when removing a metric, in order to coax the library to providing the names of labels and values. This can be very expensive when many metrics are updated at once.

Now, the integration retains all needed information for removing metrics, making removal much faster. I've confirmed that setting 1200 metrics to `unavailable` takes the same amount of time now as setting them to a value. Previously, it was approximately 10 times slower.

The logic for saving this information is in `_metrics()`, which now takes a dict of labels. This required a bit of refactoring, but I think it is overall somewhat easier to follow.

I also removed some special handling for `friendly_name` which I am pretty sure was unneeded.

No changes to tests were required.

issue_context.title: Updating a lot of states uses 100% CPU with prometheus
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When I reload the Unifi Integration, my HA completely locks up. After ssh'ing in and running a sudo docker stats I can see that the homeassistant container is using 100% CPU.

It remains at 100% CPU for about 4-5 minutes before coming back down, and then HA is responsive again.

During this time HA's web UI is completely down and its completely deadlocked.  Feels like some sort of thread locking issue.

I am running on an Intel N200 with 16GB of ram, so I have quite a bit of power behind this.

Occurs during Safe Mode as well.

I am pretty sure I see this with other integrations as well.

The logs don't appear to be helpful. During this window I'll see a bunch of network timeouts log entries, but I know the networking is not the problem (and SSH remains responsive).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.12.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Unifi Network

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/unifi/

Diagnostic info: [config_entry-unifi-01J4NC8K8GGBP3THDJSJDF799M.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18128509/config_entry-unifi-01J4NC8K8GGBP3THDJSJDF799M.json)

Ok, I've reproduced this issue with a dev version of home assistant. The issue is the `_remove_labelsets` method iterates over all metrics just to delete 1, and now metrics are deleted when they become unavailable. I'll look at making this faster, possibly by caching metrics within the component.

I downloaded your PR as a custom component and took a new profile, found here:
[callgrind.out.1734359614480680.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18151940/callgrind.out.1734359614480680.zip) (remove .zip)

Reloading Unifi is now much quicker. I saw a 100% CPU spike only for 10-15 seconds.

I have 3800 entities with the unifi integraton.
